bib.title: On the Fundamental Limits of LLMs at Scale

legacy_report:
ADDENDUM AND CORRECTIONS (supersedes my earlier report where they differ)

COVERAGE: All 67 pages (257,365 chars) of body text are now read, including Sec 2 (hallucination), Sec 4 (reasoning), Sec 6 (multimodal), Sec 7 (benchmarks), and Sec 8-9. The paper has no appendices. It ends at p. 67 with the reference list (pp. 48-67); I read only the last ~40% of the references and checked the rest by search, which is enough to trace origins. No embedded instructions found.

ASSESSMENT UNCHANGED: still theory-plus-survey with no experiments of its own. The new sections confirm it, and they are worse for rigor than the long-context section.

CORRECTIONS TO MY EARLIER REPORT
- The conclusion about retrieval and memory "can help approach these ceilings, but cannot surpass them" is on p. 47, not "p. 52-ish".
- The Theta(ln N) margin: the lemma and Corollary 1 are on pp. 19-20, and Fig 5 caption is on p. 17. My "p. 16" quote location was wrong.
- I named RULER and Hsieh et al. 2024 as a source. The paper cites Hsieh et al. 2024 only for "reordering equally scored passages alters accuracy" (p. 30), with no number. Disregard my RULER mention.
- The "70B ... 64K effective" and "<50%" numbers cite Wang et al. 2024c, which the reference list gives as "Why does the effective context length of LLMs fall short?" arXiv 2410.18745. Cite that as the origin. The paper itself attributes the 64K figure to "Grattafiori et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024c" and says it "was found". I did not verify against the originals.

NEW MATERIAL BEARING ON CONTEXT, RETRIEVAL, DILUTION, MEMORY
1. Retrieval under a token budget (Sec 5.1.1, p. 29): the constraint "sum of len(d) <= B" forces a relevance/coverage trade-off. Quote: "excessive coverage induces contextual dilution and generation drift". Fig 8 (p. 28) is a 3-D "accuracy" surface with budget iso-lines (B up to ~37,714 tokens; "best under low cost (B = 10699 tokens)"). It is a stylized illustration with no stated data source or model, so it must not be cited as an empirical result.
2. Distractor sensitivity (p. 32): "adding a single irrelevant passage can reduce accuracy by up to 30%, with degradation correlating to the distractor's cosine similarity". This is cited from Yang et al. 2025b (arXiv 2505.18761) and Amiraz et al. 2025. Related origin: Shi et al. 2023, "LLMs can be easily distracted by irrelevant context". Setup is not given in this paper, so cite the originals.
3. Softmax mixture argument (pp. 32-33): the attention-mass formulation alpha_i, and the claim that a distractor "is fused into the model's latent state, irreversibly influencing generation". This is an informal argument, not a measurement.
4. Chunking (p. 30): cross-chunk "fragmentation loss", and average similarity falling as k grows. Both are argued, not measured.
5. Lost-in-the-middle (p. 30): restated, with Liu et al. 2023c as the origin.
6. Poisoned retrieval (p. 31): "inserting only five poisoned documents per target query in million-scale KBs achieves ~90% attack success rates" (Zou et al. 2025, PoisonedRAG). RevPRAG detector "~98% true-positive rate with <2% false positives" (Tan et al. 2024).
7. Source arbitration (p. 33): the parametric-vs-context trade-off (ConflictBank, ClashEval).
8. Table 1 (p. 21) lists failure modes with mitigations. It includes "irrelevant filler dilutes signal", chunk-boundary loss, and "external memory is not persistent across tasks/sessions" (mitigation: vector DB with RAG, memory distilled from transcripts). The table is a catalogue with no data.
9. "Attention dilution" in the paper means something different (p. 38): redundant visual tokens in multimodal models. "In VideoLLaMA-7B, output tokens attend to text tokens 157 times more than to visual tokens" (from Wu et al. 2025a). This is unrelated to text context length.
10. Sec 2, 4, 6, 7 contain nothing else on context or memory.

OTHER NUMBERS SEEN (all cited, none the paper's own)
- GPT-4 factual precision below 40% for tail entities versus above 90% for popular ones (Kandpal et al. 2023).
- Web scrapes contain 2-3% false claims.
- Prompt format changes shifted accuracy by up to 40 points (He et al. 2024).
- Seed changes moved Pass@1 by 5-15 points (Hochlehnert et al. 2025).

PROBLEMS WITH RIGOR (new)
- Theorem 2's proof is flawed: it defines i_k := k mod (k+1), which equals k, so each model is hit only once, not infinitely often.
- Lemma 3 covers sinusoidal encodings only. The RoPE claim that attention is "exponentially dampened" is asserted without proof or number.
- Prop 5-7 and Eq 10 (the noise floor) are stylized or "empirically testable claims". Fig 3 (pp. 9-10) plots values cited from others, not data produced here.
- The paper is internally inconsistent about the original source of numbers, e.g. duplicated "Wang et al., 2024c;c".

ASSESSMENT: The verdict stands. It adds nothing citable beyond its sources for numbers. Citable as a labelled theoretical argument: Lemma 4 / Corollary 1 (softmax needs a ~ln N margin) and the exposure-times-attention failure bound in RAG. Treat it as a preprint under review at TMLR (arXiv v2, 26 Jan 2026). For the note, use it as "sharpens" (citation plus references row), and cite Wang 2024c, Liu 2023c, Yang 2025b / Shi 2023 and Zou 2025 for the empirical claims.
